results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if the target document is unknown)] [Prerequisite]: Locate the document using GOOGLEDRIVE_FIND_FILE (if results are empty despite success, broaden/adjust search scoping).
[Optional (if file type or access is uncertain)] [Prerequisite]: Validate it is an editable native document using GOOGLEDRIVE_GET_FILE_METADATA (confirm mimeType/permissions suitability).
[Optional (if rollback is desired before destructive edits)] [Prerequisite]: Create a backup copy using GOOGLEDOCS_COPY_DOCUMENT (store the copy identifier).

[Required] [Prerequisite]: Read current content using GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_PLAINTEXT (use document_id; confirm target, choose overwrite vs section update, and capture fresh UTF-16 indices/markers).

[Required] [Step]: Write the new Markdown using GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN (use id; full overwrite) or GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKDOWN (section update only with fresh indices from the latest read).
[Optional (for verification)] [Next Step]: Spot-check results using GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_PLAINTEXT (confirm expected headings/markers rather than inspecting update replies).
[Fallback (if section update fails with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT/invalidRange)] [Fallback]: Retry by overwriting the full body using GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN (avoids stale/incorrect indices).
known_pitfalls: [GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] May fail on empty or whitespace-only Markdown; require meaningful content.
[GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] Success responses can include a very large "replies" array with many empty objects; verify via GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_PLAINTEXT instead.
[GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN] Certain Markdown constructs can cause unintended broad bold styling; rely on readback markers to detect presentation issues early.
[GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_SECTION_MARKDOWN] Range edits require correct UTF-16 startIndex/endIndex; stale indices commonly trigger 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT/invalidRange.
[GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_PLAINTEXT] Readback may truncate long documents and can intermittently return HTTP 502; retry with backoff and verify using distinctive markers.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Find paragraph start/end indices that contain a token (helps choose section ranges).
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
content=doc['body']['content']
for it in content:
    p=it.get('paragraph')
    if not p: continue
    txt=''.join(e.get('textRun',{}).get('content','') for e in p.get('elements',[]))
    if 'TOKEN' in txt: print(it.get('startIndex'),it.get('endIndex'),txt.strip())
```

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Compute a safe end insertion index from a document structure response.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
content=doc['body']['content']
end_index=max(b.get('endIndex',0) for b in content)
print(end_index-1)
```

GOOGLEDOCS_UPDATE_DOCUMENT_MARKDOWN.description: Replaces the entire content of an existing Google Docs document with new Markdown text; requires edit permissions for the document.

id.description: The unique identifier for the Google Docs document to update. Accepts either a document ID (alphanumeric string, length varies by document age - newer documents typically have 44-character IDs) or a full Google Docs URL (e.g., https://docs.google.com/document/d/{DOCUMENT_ID}/edit). When a URL is provided, the document ID will be automatically extracted.

tab_id.description: Optional tab ID to replace with the rendered Markdown. When omitted, the first tab is updated.

examples:
# Document Title

This is a paragraph with **bold** and *italic* text.

- Unordered list item 1
- Unordered list item 2

1. Ordered list item 1
2. Ordered list item 2

An image: ![Alt text for image](https://www.example.com/image.png)

## Advanced Markdown


# Example Python code
def greet(name):
    print(f'Hello, {name}!')
greet('World')


| Column A | Column B |
|----------|----------|
|   Data 1 |   Data 2 |
|   Data 3 |   Data 4 |

> This is a blockquote.
markdown.description: Markdown content that will replace the document's entire existing content. Supports standard Markdown features.

GOOGLEDOCS_GET_DOCUMENT_PLAINTEXT.description: Retrieve a Google Doc by ID and return a best-effort plain-text rendering. Converts document structure into plain text including paragraphs, lists, and tables without requiring clients to traverse complex Docs API JSON.

tab_ids.description: Optional tab IDs to include when include_tabs_content=true. Nested child tabs are searched recursively.

document_id.description: The unique identifier for the Google Document. Accepts either a document ID (typically a 44-character alphanumeric string) or a full Google Docs URL. When a URL is provided, the document ID will be automatically extracted. Note: This parameter also accepts 'id' as an alias for consistency with other GOOGLEDOCS tools.

include_tables.description: Whether to include table content in the plain text output. Tables are rendered with configurable cell and row delimiters.

include_footers.description: Whether to include footer text in the plain text output. Footers are appended with a clear section separator.

include_headers.description: Whether to include header text in the plain text output. Headers are appended with a clear section separator.

include_footnotes.description: Whether to include footnote text in the plain text output. Footnotes are appended with a clear section separator.

table_row_delimiter.description: The delimiter to use between table rows (default: newline character).

include_tabs_content.description: When true, fetch the document using includeTabsContent=true query parameter to render all tabs. When false, only the main body content is rendered.

table_cell_delimiter.description: The delimiter to use between table cells (default: tab character).

GOOGLEDOCS_COPY_DOCUMENT.description: Tool to create a copy of an existing Google Document. Use this to duplicate a document, for example, when using an existing document as a template. The copied document will have a default title (e.g., 'Copy of [original title]') if no new title is provided, and will be placed in the user's root Google Drive folder.

title.description: The title for the new copied document. If not provided, the title will be 'Copy of [original document's title]'.

document_id.description: The ID of the Google Document to be copied.

include_shared_drives.description: Whether to support copying documents from shared drives. Defaults to True.
